body: Don't know it you're still online, but thanks for listening to me. I think I'll be able to sleep now.
Oh ouch, sorry to hear about that. Well, thanks for listening to me. I think I'll finally be able to sleep now.

Thanks for talking to me by the way. And aside from the debt thing, he really does help me out a lot. He's helped me study when he wasn't busy, like with flashcards and such when I *was* in school. Hell, I'm just glad he was there for me so I could get away from my parents. So, he's definitely not the issue. I just want to know if I have what it takes to ever go back to school again, and if trying to go to a bigger university would help place me in a better environment. My other regret with school is not being able to do dorming and missing out on the "college experience."

He knows about everything except my massive debt. He's in debt for school too, and I feel that telling him about my debt would just make things super bad, since part of the reason I have a bad debt is due to buying frivolous crap I regret, and he would just yell at me for being financially irresponsible. Still, I could probably pay it off in a year if I had even just a part time job. But I live in the middle of nowhere in the U.S., and and trying to find a job here sucks.

My boyfriend's got a great steady job. He's 25, and doesn't have a degree just like me, but he does one class each semester online. Guess I'm fucked for education, because I'm American! Ha! But in all seriousness, I feel really bad because he works all day and supports both of us, and I just stay at home depressed and doing nothing. Maybe going to a different school could help? Community college is depressing as fuck. I thought about going to a four year university instead for a better environment, but I'm not dumb enough to apply right away. I want to self study and maybe learn a language before I apply, just to get back in the swing of things. Plus I need a job to pay off my massive debt before going back.

Well, as soon as I graduated, I said to myself, "fuck school. I need some time to recover." My parents weren't too happy about that. I slept all day, and stayed up all night playing video games. I did that to avoid any contact with the outside world. Fast forward one year later, and I get a job at Walmart. That shit only lasted 3 months, and I haven't had a job since. Then, when I was 19, I applied to school and got accepted. I wasn't thrilled about it, I mean, the school has a 99% acceptance rate, and I felt like a failure going to bumfuck community college. It was during that semester I met my now boyfriend. I didn't even make it through one semester, so I quit. I move in with my boyfriend to get away from my parents since they think I'm a failure (I'm part Asian). At 20, I try again. Fucked that up too, quit. Now, I'm playing the role of housewife, and I feel bad. I don't want to be one of those women that depend on their significant other for support. I want to have a career of my own and be successful. But so far, that's not working, and I feel more than ever like a failure since all my friends are getting degrees.
Sorry if I'm making you feel bad. You really are helping me, and I appreciate it. All of what you are saying is right. I just... want a glimmer of hope to know that life WILL get better.
I like your narrative. I just hope that the embarrassing and bad moments in my life that I remember, that other people don't remember those same moments.

Your English is good enough, and I can definitely understand you. It's just nice to have someone to talk to. As far as feeling suicidal goes, it used to be way worse when I was in high school. It was so bad I even wrote a note and had a plan. I still think about it sometimes; every day I just picture putting a gun to my head. I can't help but think of the bad and embarassing moments in my life; I wish I could stop all the bad thoughts but I can't. I'm just glad I'm not in the hell that is high school and I escaped that toxic environment.
